principles: The action purpose chooses the component; a legacy appearance never creates a new variant.
Theme, density, viewport, content language and interaction state are contexts rather than variants.
Danger communicates a destructive consequence and is never decorative.
Toggle behavior communicates a persistent pressed state and cannot be combined with danger or primary hierarchy.
Icon-only actions require an accessible action name and use the project-owned Lucide semantic icon interface.

legacyCoverage.rule: Legacy counts prove coverage and scenario demand; they do not define target variants or appearance.

runtimeContract.engineBoundary: Business pages consume only ic-* tags, semantic attributes and --ui-* Tokens; Web Awesome remains internal.
runtimeContract.iconLanguage: ic-icon semantic names backed by the fixed local Lucide release
runtimeContract.iconButtonBackground: background=ghost stays transparent and strengthens only the icon on hover; hierarchy=primary provides the reusable primary icon action surface.

components.purpose: Trigger a labeled product action with constrained hierarchy, consequence tone and optional persistent toggle behavior.
useWhen: The visible label names the action.
The action submits or resets a form.
A persistent pressed state is clearer as a labeled toggle action than as a selection field.
invariants: A region should expose at most one primary action at the same hierarchy level.
ghost is a presentation of the secondary neutral action: its default surface is transparent and its hover surface is --ui-color-action-tertiary-hover; ic-icon-button does not support ghost.
Secondary neutral, secondary ghost and secondary danger buttons use --ui-font-weight-regular and preserve their default foreground color on hover.
pressed is valid only when toggle is present.
toggle buttons use type=button and do not submit forms.
loading prevents repeated activation and exposes a named busy state.
Disabled and loading are states, never variants.

components.purpose: Trigger a compact action whose only visible content is one project semantic icon.
useWhen: The icon meaning is established in the immediate professional-tool context.
Space is constrained in a toolbar, Canvas overlay or repeated row action.
invariants: label is always the accessible action name and is never optional.
shortcut is optional Tooltip metadata and never replaces label as the accessible action name.
tooltip-disabled suppresses the generated Tooltip without changing the control's accessible name.
Button size maps to the shared control-height and icon-size tokens automatically: xs 20/10/12, small 28/12/16, medium 36/14/20, large 40/16/24; medium is the default.
The square control box remains circular with round corner geometry; it does not use the squircle shape reserved for non-circular buttons.
The xs icon uses a 1px stroke so the smallest control remains legible; larger icon buttons keep their size-specific stroke tokens.
background=ghost removes the base fill and border in every theme; hover strengthens only the icon color by one semantic step from --ui-color-text-tertiary to --ui-color-text-secondary.
hierarchy=primary provides the reusable primary icon action used by Composer run controls; the Actions family owns its fill, hover, shadow and icon stroke.
icon accepts only semantic names from ic-icon.
Primary ic-icon-button actions require a non-empty label attribute for their accessible name and Tooltip.
Danger icon actions remain quiet so destructive meaning does not become decorative emphasis.

components.purpose: Trigger video playback from a cover using the Figma-defined circular play treatment.
useWhen: A video cover needs the product-standard play action before the native player is visible.
invariants: medium is the default and renders the Figma main-controller treatment at 4rem.
small renders the same asset at 32px for thumbnail video covers.
label is always forwarded to the internal native button as its accessible action name.
The action only enters playback; browser-native video controls remain responsible for playback after activation.

components.purpose: Give related actions one accessible group name and one visual relationship without taking over their individual semantics.
useWhen: Two or more adjacent actions operate on the same object or task.
Toolbar actions need one announced group name.
invariants: The group does not change child hierarchy, tone, state or form behavior.
A group contains at most one primary action.
Selection widgets use their dedicated component family rather than button-group.
